A spreadsheet like Google Sheets or Excel. `pz.Workbook` holds the data and computes the
formulas, `pz.sheet` draws the grid and `ui.Spreadsheet` adds a toolbar, menus and sheet
tabs. See the [Spreadsheet section](/pyzed/spreadsheet/).

```python
book = pz.Workbook()
book["A1"], book["A2"], book["A3"] = 2, 3, "=A1*A2"
ui.Spreadsheet(book=book)
```

## Workbook

### `Workbook`

```python
class Workbook
```

A spreadsheet workbook: sheets of cells with values, formulas and formats.

Read and write cells by address (`book["B2"] = "=SUM(A1:A9)"`; `book["A1:C3"]` gives
rows of values), format them, sort, filter, undo, and open or save CSV and Excel files.
Show it (and edit it) with `ui.Spreadsheet(book=book)` or `pz.sheet(book)`. Addresses may name a sheet
(`"Sales!A1"`); without one they use the active sheet. Row and column numbers are
1-based, as in the grid; columns are also accepted as letters (`"C"`).

```python
book = pz.Workbook(sheets=["Sales", "Team"])
book["Sales!B2"] = "=SUM(C2:C9)"
book.format("A1:G1", bold=True, fill="#e8f0fe")
book.save("report.xlsx")
```

Every method is described in [The workbook in Python](/pyzed/spreadsheet/workbook/), [Formatting](/pyzed/spreadsheet/formatting/), [Sort, filter and validate](/pyzed/spreadsheet/data/), [Rows, columns and sheets](/pyzed/spreadsheet/structure/) and [Files](/pyzed/spreadsheet/files/); `help(pz.Workbook)` lists them with their docstrings.

**Methods and properties**

#### `Workbook.open`

```python
@staticmethod
Workbook.open(path)
```

Opens a file: `.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.xls`, `.ods`, `.csv`, `.tsv` or `.txt`.

#### `Workbook.from_bytes`

```python
@staticmethod
Workbook.from_bytes(data)
```

A workbook from an Excel or OpenDocument file's bytes.

#### `Workbook.from_csv`

```python
@staticmethod
Workbook.from_csv(text, delimiter=None)
```

A workbook from CSV (or TSV) text. `delimiter=None` guesses it.

#### `Workbook.from_rows`

```python
@staticmethod
Workbook.from_rows(rows, *, header=None, sheet=None)
```

A workbook from rows of values (lists, or dicts whose keys become the header row).

#### `Workbook.functions`

```python
@staticmethod
Workbook.functions()
```

The functions formulas can use: `[(name, arguments, description), ...]`.

#### `Workbook.column_name`

```python
@staticmethod
Workbook.column_name(col)
```

The column letters of a 1-based number (`column_name(28) == "AB"`).

## Showing it

### `Spreadsheet`

```python
class Spreadsheet
```

A component: the whole spreadsheet, with the grid and its formula bar, a toolbar, right-click menus, a find bar, panels for conditional formatting, validation and notes, sheet tabs and a status bar with the selection's sum. Everything the user does goes to `book`. See [The Spreadsheet component](/pyzed/spreadsheet/component/).

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `book` | The `pz.Workbook` to show and edit (a new empty one when `None`). Keep it in your app so its data survives view rebuilds. |
| `toolbar` | Shows the toolbar. |
| `formula_bar` | Shows the name box and the formula bar. |
| `tabs` | Shows the sheet tabs and the status bar. |
| `headers` | Shows the column letters and row numbers. |
| `readonly` | Users can select, copy and find, but not change anything. |
| `text_size` | Pixel size of 10 pt text. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `on_change` | Receives `event.value` with `action`, `range` and `sheet` when the user changes something. |
| `on_select` | Receives `event.value` with `range` and `sheet` when the selection changes. |

```python
ui.Spreadsheet(book=self.book, on_change=lambda e: print(e.value.action, e.value.range))
```

### `sheet`

```python
sheet(
    book,
    *,
    colors=None,
    text_size=13.0,
    formula_bar=True,
    headers=True,
    width=None,
    height=None,
    readonly=False,
    on_change=None,
    on_select=None,
    on_context=None,
    on_dropdown=None,
    on_filter=None,
    on_find=None,
    on_invalid=None,
    on_edit=None,
)
```

The spreadsheet grid on its own: cells, headers and formula bar, with selection, editing, formulas, the fill handle, copy and paste and the keyboard shortcuts of Sheets and Excel. It draws only the cells in view. The grid doesn't draw menus: its events say where the user clicked. See [The grid on its own](/pyzed/spreadsheet/grid/).

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `book` | The `pz.Workbook` to show. |
| `colors` | A dict of colors (`background`, `grid`, `header`, `text`, `accent`, `selection`...); `ui.sheet_colors(theme)` makes one from a theme. |
| `text_size` | Pixel size of 10 pt text. |
| `formula_bar` | Shows the name box and the formula bar. |
| `headers` | Shows the column letters and row numbers. |
| `width` | Width: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `height` | Height: pixels, `"fill"`, `"shrink"` or `"fill:N"` (proportion). |
| `readonly` | Select and copy only. |
| `on_change` | Called with a dict when the user changes cells, formats or the structure: `action` (`"edit"`, `"paste"`, `"fill"`, `"clear"`, `"format"`, `"sort"`, `"undo"`...), `range` and `sheet`. |
| `on_select` | Called with a dict when the selection changes (read `book.selection`). |
| `on_context` | Called on a right click with `kind` (`"cell"`, `"row"` or `"column"`), `cell`, `x` and `y` (relative to the grid): show a menu there. |
| `on_dropdown` | Called when a list cell's dropdown should open: `cell`, `options`, `x`, `y`, `width`. |
| `on_filter` | Called when a filter button of the header is clicked: `column`, `x`, `y`. |
| `on_find` | Called on Ctrl+F or Ctrl+H: `mode` (`"find"` or `"replace"`). |
| `on_invalid` | Called when a typed value breaks a strict validation rule: `cell`, `value`, `message`. |
| `on_edit` | Called when typing in a cell starts or ends: `editing`. |

```python
pz.sheet(self.book, formula_bar=False, on_change=lambda e: print(e["action"], e["range"]))
```

### `sheet_colors`

```python
sheet_colors(theme=None)
```

The colors `ui.Spreadsheet` gives its grid for a theme, as the dict `pz.sheet(colors=...)` takes.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `theme` | A theme (the current one by default). |
